gaps.sentence: The phone is ringing. Don't worry, I ___ it.
gaps.hint: a spontaneous decision at the moment
gaps.explanation: Decisions made at the moment of speaking use 'will': will answer.

gaps.sentence: They ___ for two hours when the storm hit.
gaps.hint: two hours of walking before the storm
gaps.explanation: A duration leading up to a past moment takes the past perfect continuous: had been walking.

gaps.sentence: When I came downstairs, the whole house ___ of fresh bread.
gaps.hint: smell as a state verb in past
gaps.explanation: 'Smell' as a state verb takes simple tenses, here the past simple: smelled.

gaps.sentence: It is the first time I ___ paella.
gaps.hint: it is the first time takes present perfect
gaps.explanation: After 'It is the first time', English uses the present perfect: have eaten.

gaps.sentence: I can't talk now — I ___ dinner for twelve people.
gaps.hint: now plus a temporary activity in progress
gaps.explanation: 'Now' marks a temporary action in progress, so the present continuous is needed: am cooking.

gaps.sentence: Don't worry about the dog — it ___ at strangers, but it never bites.
gaps.hint: typical behavior takes the present simple
gaps.explanation: Characteristic, repeated behavior takes the present simple: barks.

gaps.sentence: When I got to the office, I realised I ___ my security pass.
gaps.hint: the forgetting happened before realising it
gaps.explanation: The forgetting happened before the past moment of realising, so the past perfect is needed: had forgotten.

gaps.sentence: By Friday, the climbers ___ on the north face for six days without a break.
gaps.hint: duration measured to a future point
gaps.explanation: 'By Friday + for six days' calls for the future perfect: will have been.
